title: EA-PREDICTION-INDEX-01 — The Prediction Index of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Method, Locations, Organization and Contents (4,394 Claims in 194 Subject Pages)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The prediction index of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, described and rehearsed: 4,394 claims — 1,026 forecasts, 950 standing claims, 1,029 unbuilt tests, 1,088 historical theses, 301 priority records — read out of every deposit's seated text, the own-voice fields of the two large datasets, the text the record repair added and the attachments, quoted verbatim and checked against the texts, grouped into 194 subject pages on operativesemiotics.org and published as a dataset in Alexanarch. Each claim registers at its earliest stated statement; every statement carries four dates kept apart (stated, attested, interpreted, indexed). Speculative specifications carry their mode and what fulfilment would be; standing claims carry their falsifier kind, the source's condition kept apart from a reader's; confirmation records are attached as evidence and marked first-party where they are, with no verdict given. A second reading of forty random deposits by another model measured recall at 0.945. Every claim has a stable route; this deposit anchors build PI-2026-10-18-9b0e16492f. The document gives the method, the locations, the organization, and the index itself, page by page.
content_type: Dataset; the description of the prediction index, with the index rehearsed
substrate: AI-assisted. The sweep, the second reading pass, triage, grouping, naming, the annotation, describe and recall passes were carried out in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) and parallel Claude readers under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction, each reader recording its own provenance; the recall audit's second reading was by a different Claude model. Every quotation was verified mechanically against the deposit texts. This description was drafted in session from the index's own files, circulated for review (ChatGPT, Kimi), and revised on their reports, which Lee Sharks adopted.
methodology: The sweep (2026-10-15) read 1,616 deposits in full; pass 2 (2026-10-18) read the text the record repair added and the attachments; every find quoted verbatim and verified against the text by script. Triage, topical and join passes grouped 6,305 finds into 4,394 claims; communities in the claims' link graph, read and named by readers, made 194 pages. On the reviews of the draft: an annotation pass dated every statement of 1,283 claims and gave modes and falsifier kinds; a describe pass rewrote every page description to attribute its claims; a recall audit re-read 40 random deposits with a different model and brief and adjudicated every unmatched passage. Protocols: data/reading/READING-PROTOCOL.md, TRIAGE-PROTOCOL.md, ANNOTATION-PROTOCOL.md, RECALL-BRIEF.md, RECALL-ADJUDICATE.md; data/index/NAMING-, REVIEW-, DESCRIBE-PROTOCOL.md.
falsification_conditions: The index is falsified at a claim if its quotation is not verbatim at its lines in the text it names, or its dates do not match the text's own dating where the text gives one; at a file if the file does not match the SHA-256 this document gives for build PI-2026-10-18-9b0e16492f; and in its coverage figure if a larger random second reading finds required passages the sweep missed at a rate inconsistent with recall 0.945.
axn_reading: Duration -> Closure -> Origin -> Foundation -> Text -> Closure
wiki_article:
EA-PREDICTION-INDEX-01 describes and rehearses the prediction index of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: 4,394 claims read out of the archive's deposits — every deposit's seated text in full (1,616 deposits, about ten million words), the own-voice fields of its two large datasets, the text its record repair added and its attachments — quoted verbatim, checked against the texts by script, and grouped into 194 subject pages on operativesemiotics.org, with the whole published as a dataset in Alexanarch. The claims fall into five tiers: forecasts (1,026), standing claims about how systems behave (950), unbuilt tests (1,029), historical theses (1,088) and priority records (301); 401 confirmation records, the deposits' own claims that an earlier prediction came true or failed, are attached as evidence without a verdict.

The document was circulated in draft and revised on two reviews. Each statement now carries four dates kept apart — when its words were written, when it was publicly attested, when it interprets something earlier, and when the index recorded it — and a claim registers at its earliest stated statement, so a 2026 foreword no longer takes the date of the 2014 letters it introduces. Speculative specifications carry their mode (fictional report, design specification, scenario, performative anticipation, vision) and what fulfilment would mean; standing claims carry their falsifier kind, with the source's condition kept apart from a reader's. A second reading of forty random deposits by another model, adjudicated against the sweep protocol, measured recall at 0.945. Every claim has a stable route, and the deposit anchors one build of the dataset by its id and hashes.
